newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: DCC says buys Merits for $4.18 mln.
newsitem.headline: DCC says buys Merits for $4.18 mln.

text.p: Irish-based industrial holding company DCC Plc said on Monday it had acquired a 45 percent interest in Merits Health Products Company for a cash consideration of $4.18 million.
DCC also announced the acquisition of the wholesale division of wine merchants Mitchell and Son of Dublin by Woodford Bourne, the wholesale wine subsidiary of DCC Foods, for 0.55 million punts.
DCC said in a statement $3.34 million of the Merits purchase price would be paid into the company in respect of new shares and the remainder to existing shareholders.

Based in Taiwan with a distribution subsidiary in the United States, Merits is a manufacturer of manual and powered wheelchairs, electric scooters and other mobility and rehabilitation products, DCC said.

"Mobility and rehabilitation products now constitute the largest part of DCC Healthcare's business and the acquisition of 45 percent of Merits is an important further step in the build-up of an international business in this area," DCC said.

DCC said the acquisition of Merits will provide DCC Healthcare and its UK-based mobility products subsidiary, Days Medical Aids Limited, with a strategic alliance with a Far Eastern manufacturer of mobility and rehabilitation products.
"The link with Merits will secure for DCC Healthcare access to lower cost manufacturing in Taiwan together with a platform for the future development of a manufacturing base in China," DCC said.
"It will also provide a distribution network in the United States," he added.
